title: Festivals of light
examples: Why do Hindus light lamps at Diwali?
Why does a Hanukkah menorah have nine branches?

explain.say: In many faiths, light is a symbol of goodness, knowledge and hope shining in the dark. Four great festivals of light are Diwali, Hanukkah, Christmas and Vesak.

Diwali is celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains in October or November. Hindus light rows of clay lamps called diyas; many remember Rama and Sita returning home to Ayodhya, and pray to Lakshmi, goddess of good fortune.

draw.a: Hindus: Rama's return, Lakshmi puja. Sikhs: Bandi Chhor Divas, Guru Hargobind's release. Jains: Mahavira's liberation. Light over darkness, good over evil.

draw.text: Diyas: small clay oil lamps placed in rows.

explain.say: Hanukkah is the Jewish festival of eight nights. It remembers the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem, and the story of a little oil that lasted eight days. Each night one more candle is lit on the menorah.

draw.label: branches: eight nights plus the shamash helper candle

draw.text: Families eat foods fried in oil, like latkes and doughnuts, and play with a dreidel.

explain.say: Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus, whom Christians call the light of the world. Candles, an Advent wreath and lights on trees and windows fill the dark weeks of December.

items: Jesus called the light of the world
Advent wreath: a candle each Sunday
25 December; many Orthodox churches on 7 January

explain.say: Vesak is the most important Buddhist festival, at the full moon in April or May. Many Buddhists remember the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and passing, and light lamps and lanterns as a sign of the light of wisdom.

draw.text: Lanterns, lamps, offerings and acts of kindness.

explain.say: Side by side, the four festivals tell different stories, yet the light means something similar in each: good overcoming darkness, hope, and the presence of the sacred.

faq.q: Why do Hindus light lamps at Diwali?
faq.a: Hindus light rows of small clay lamps called diyas to show light winning over darkness and good over evil. Many remember the story of Rama and Sita returning to Ayodhya after defeating the demon king Ravana, when people lit lamps to welcome them, and they invite Lakshmi, goddess of good fortune, into their homes.
asks: why are diyas lit on Diwali
what is the story of Diwali

faq.a: Diwali celebrates the victory of light over darkness. For many Hindus it marks Rama's return and honours Lakshmi; Sikhs celebrate Bandi Chhor Divas, the release of Guru Hargobind from prison; and Jains remember Mahavira reaching final liberation. It lasts up to five days with lamps, sweets, gifts and fireworks.

Sikhs celebrate Bandi Chhor Divas, the Day of Liberation, at Diwali time. It remembers Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru, being freed from prison in Gwalior Fort and insisting that fifty-two imprisoned kings be freed with him. The Golden Temple in Amritsar is lit up beautifully.

Hanukkah is a Jewish festival of eight nights, usually in December. It remembers the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem more than 2,000 years ago, after the Maccabees won it back, and the story that a single day's oil kept the Temple lamp burning for eight days.
asks: what do Jews celebrate at Hanukkah

faq.q: Why does a Hanukkah menorah have nine branches?
faq.a: The Hanukkah menorah, also called a hanukkiah, has eight branches for the eight nights, plus a ninth for the shamash, the helper candle used to light the others. One more candle is added each night until all eight burn on the last night.
asks: how many candles on a menorah

faq.q: Why is Christmas a festival of light?
faq.a: Christians call Jesus the light of the world, so at Christmas they celebrate his birth with candles, lights, stars and Advent wreaths. In the northern half of the world it also falls in the darkest weeks of the year.
asks: why are there lights at Christmas

faq.a: Vesak, also called Buddha Day, is the most important festival for many Buddhists, held on the full moon of the month of Vesakha, in April or May. It remembers the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and passing, with lanterns, temple visits, offerings and acts of kindness.
asks: what do Buddhists celebrate at Vesak

faq.q: Why is light a symbol in so many religions?
faq.a: Light lets us see, keeps us warm and drives away the dark, so it naturally stands for goodness, knowledge, hope and the sacred. Many faiths use the same picture in different ways: wisdom for Buddhists, the divine presence for Hindus and Jews, and Jesus for Christians.
Diwali falls in October or November, on a new moon night set by the Hindu lunar calendar. Because that calendar follows the moon, Diwali's date in the everyday calendar changes each year.

faq.q: Why do Jews eat fried food at Hanukkah?
faq.a: Because the festival remembers the miracle of the oil, families enjoy foods fried in oil, such as latkes, which are potato pancakes, and sufganiyot, which are jam doughnuts. Children also play with a spinning top called a dreidel.

faq.q: Are there other festivals of light?
faq.a: Yes. The Lantern Festival ends the Lunar New Year celebrations in China, Buddhists in Korea fill streets with lotus lanterns for the Buddha's birthday, and Christians in many places celebrate Candlemas. Each uses light to mark hope and new beginnings.

faq.q: Why do Diwali, Hanukkah and Christmas all happen in winter?
faq.a: They follow different calendars and remember different events, so it is partly coincidence. Still, many people point out that festivals of light feel especially meaningful in the darkest part of the year in the northern hemisphere, where these faiths began.
asks: why are light festivals in winter
do light festivals happen at the same time

facts: Diwali is celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains, usually in October or November, on a new moon night set by the Hindu lunar calendar.
Sikhs celebrate Bandi Chhor Divas at Diwali, remembering Guru Hargobind's release from Gwalior Fort.
Hanukkah lasts eight nights, and its menorah has nine branches: eight for the nights and one for the shamash.
Vesak, on the full moon of April or May, remembers the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and passing.
Many Orthodox Christian churches celebrate Christmas on 7 January, following the older Julian calendar.

quiz.say: Recall. For how many nights is Hanukkah celebrated?
quiz.show: How many nights does Hanukkah last?
quiz.why: Hanukkah lasts eight nights, remembering the oil that burned for eight days; the menorah has eight branches plus the shamash.

wrong.0: Three is too few: one candle is added each night for eight nights.
wrong.1: Five days is the length of Diwali in many places, not Hanukkah.
wrong.3: Twelve is the number of days of Christmas in some Christian traditions.

quiz.say: Apply. A family lights clay lamps, makes sweets and remembers Rama returning to Ayodhya. Which festival is it?
quiz.show: Clay lamps and Rama's return: which festival?
quiz.why: Diyas, sweets and the story of Rama and Sita's homecoming are at the heart of the Hindu celebration of Diwali.

wrong.0: Vesak is the Buddhist festival remembering the Buddha's life.
wrong.2: Hanukkah is Jewish and remembers the Temple in Jerusalem.

quiz.say: Think. Diwali, Hanukkah, Christmas and Vesak tell very different stories. What does light stand for in all of them?
quiz.show: What does the light mean across these festivals?
quiz.why: In each festival light is a symbol of goodness, hope, wisdom or the sacred shining in the dark, even though the stories differ.

wrong.1: Most of these festivals fall in autumn or winter, not at the start of summer.
wrong.2: The lights are symbols with religious meaning, nothing to do with saving energy.
